title: Priming Index and Fidelity Curation Playbook
author: Ava Thompson
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the Priming Index — a compact, service-level artifact used to summarize context-priming sensitivity and per-slice fidelity risk for production prompt families. The Priming Index ties together prompt-set metadata, eval-harness measurements, quantization sensitivity vectors, and triage rules used during model rollouts and regression investigations.

Scope: Applied ML teams, model-onboarding leads, and SRE/ops responsible for rollout coordination. This is intended to be used during: onboarding -> shadowing -> canary -> general rollout and for triaging fidelity regressions post-deploy.

Quick summary of deliverables
- Priming Index JSON schema (compact metadata to live alongside model-version artifacts).
- Fidelity curation rubric (graded actions by index score).
- Eval-harness integration steps for measuring index components (sampling, seeds, and variance budget).
- Quant-sensitivity guidance: crosswalk between index bands and quant profiles.
- Regression triage playbook: escalation ladder, rollback gates, and automated blames.

Definitions
- Priming: any prompt or session history used to bias model output. Includes single-turn instructions and multi-turn system-state.
- Priming Index (PI): 0..100 integer that captures combined sensitivity across four axes: context-sensitivity, semantic-variance, token-economy exposure, and quant-fragility.
- Fidelity: operational measure of response correctness/coherence relative to golden annotations or slice-level metrics.

Index calculation (high-level)
1) For a given prompt-family, collect N = 1,000 stratified probes (from workload fingerprinting).
2) Run eval-harness under three conditions: baseline float32, target-quant, and simulated-prefix-loss.
3) Compute per-probe deltas: semantic-score-delta, embedding-stability-delta, length-token-delta, and nll-delta.
4) Normalize deltas per-axis to 0..1, weight axes (default weights: context 0.35, semantic 0.35, token-economy 0.15, quant 0.15) and sum -> PI (0..1) then scale to 0..100.

PI Banding and recommended actions
- 0–20 (Low): no additional constraints. Auto-rollout allowed. Record index in model artifact metadata.
- 21–45 (Moderate): recommend shadow testing for 24–72 hours with golden-annotator sampling. If drift > threshold (see SLOs below) require A/B canary.
- 46–75 (High): require human review of 200 probes, quant-fallback allowed; hold for manual signoff. 
- 76–100 (Critical): block auto-rollout. Require dedicated canary with tenant isolation and rollback guardrails. Consider model variant or prompt rewrite.

Fidelity curation rubric (examples)
- Semantic continuity loss: semantic-score-delta > 0.12 on median -> escalate to Applied ML oncall and mark as high.
- Hallucination spike: truth-aligned F1 drop > 8% -> create incident classification "Fidelity-High" and start triage.
- Embedding drift: embedding cosine-stability < 0.92 across quant variants -> require mixed-precision fallback.

Integration with eval harness
Prereqs: access to eval-cluster, evaluator CLI v2.8+, artifact registry with model-version and priming-index field.
Measurement steps:
1. Checkout reference probe set: evaluator get-primer --service <service> --family <family> --seed 42 --size 1000
2. Run baseline: evaluator run --model <model:v> --mode baseline --metric-set fidelity,embed,perplexity --out /tmp/baseline.json
3. Run quant target: evaluator run --model <model:v> --quant-profile <profile> --out /tmp/quant.json
4. Run simulated loss: evaluator run --model <model:v> --inject-prefix-loss 0.03 --out /tmp/prefix_loss.json
5. Summarize: evaluator summarize --inputs /tmp/*.json --schema priming-index-default --output priming-index.json

Example priming-index.json fields (compact view)
| field | description | example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| family | logical prompt family id | "checkout-summary-v2" |
| sample_size | number of probes used | "1000" |
| context_sensitivity | normalized axis value 0..1 | "0.42" |
| semantic_variance | normalized axis value 0..1 | "0.37" |
| token_exposure | normalized axis value 0..1 | "0.11" |
| quant_fragility | normalized axis value 0..1 | "0.09" |
| priming_index | 0..100 integer | "39" |

Quantization crosswalk (recommended mappings)
- PI 0–20 -> Aggressive quant profile allowed (q4_0, q3mix) with standard shadow monitor.
- PI 21–45 -> Conservative quant (q4_1) and enable quant-fallback shards for 5% of traffic.
- PI 46–75 -> Mixed precision with per-slice fallback routing; require golden-anchored human review in rollout.
- PI 76–100 -> No quantized rollout; require float variant or model change.

Monitoring SLOs and alerting hooks
- SLOs to attach to services using Priming Index:
  - fidelity.delta.median <= 0.06 (alert: Sev3)
  - hallucination.rate <= 0.02 (alert: Sev2)
  - embedding.cosine.stability >= 0.92 (alert: Sev3)
  - quant-fallback-rate <= 0.05 (alert: Info)
- Alerting wiring: index-based alerts emitted to #applied-ml-alerting and to PagerDuty APPLIED-ML oncall if any of the Sev2 or above conditions are violated. Include priming-index metadata in the alert payload.

Onboarding checklist (for a new prompt family)
1. Register prompt-family in the priming registry (CLI: primingctl register --family <id> --owner <team>).
2. Attach initial probe set (size >= 500; prefer 1k).
3. Run priming-index measurement (eval-harness integration above).
4. Review PI and follow banding actions.
5. If PI > 45, schedule human-in-the-loop review and annotate 200 golden probes.
6. For quant rollouts, perform shadow-traffic run for 48–72 hours, compare deltas, and record metrics.

Regression triage playbook (fast path)
1. Detection: automated monitor fires (fidelity.delta.median breach) with priming-index attached.
2. Fast-collect: run evaluator subset for the latest 500 requests and generate per-probe deltas (command: evaluator quick-run --last 500 --family <family> --out /tmp/quick.json).
3. Hypothesis scoring: apply probabilistic-blame model (see related_pages) to rank likely causes (prompt-change, model-weight-change, quant-shift, infra).
4. Mitigation ladder:
   a) If quant-related and PI < 46 -> enable quant-fallback for affected shards (config: rollout.fallback=true).
   b) If prompt drift suspected -> disable recent prompt rewrites and revert to last stable prompt bundle.
   c) If model change suspected -> roll back to previous version and re-run priming-index on both versions.
5. Postmortem: capture delta matrix, PI history, and remediation steps. Tag incident with "fidelity-regression" and attach automated artifact (priming-index.json).

Ownership and governance
- Priming Index service owner: Applied ML Platform (team contact: applied-ml-platform@redwood.com).
- Oncall: Applied ML SRE rotation responsible for alerts.
- Review cadence: Quarterly audit of priming-index weightings and thresholds.

Implementation notes and tradeoffs
- Weight choices: default weights are opinionated and reflect production signal studies; teams may override weights for specialized workloads but must record weight overrides in the priming-index artifact.
- Sample size vs cost: N=1,000 gives stable estimates for median deltas; smaller services may use N=200 with increased variance budget and stricter banding.
- Privacy: probe sets containing customer data must be redacted and run under privacy sandbox. See related_pages for privacy playbooks.

Appendices
A. Sample CLI snippets
- Register family:
  primingctl register --family checkout-summary-v2 --owner payments-team --description "order summary prompts"
- Generate index (fast):
  primingctl measure --model production-llm:2026-08 --family checkout-summary-v2 --size 1000 --out priming-index.json

B. Example remediation checklist (for PI=58)
1. Hold rollout.
2. Create golden annotation task for 200 probes.
3. Run quant-fallback shadow for 72h.
4. Present findings at Daily Ops review and require product signoff.

C. Change log
- 2026-02-10: Initial draft (A. Thompson)
- 2026-05-12: Added quant crosswalk and monitoring SLOs (reviewers: D. Morales)

If you need a workload-specific template (PI calculation spreadsheet, evaluator job template, or priming-index JSON schema), ping Applied ML Platform and we will provision a sandbox with sample artifacts.
